question: What is mainland China's current legal and operating perimeter for private virtual currency, RWA tokenization and e-CNY; what are the six large state-owned and systemically important banks actually doing as e-CNY operators; what changed in the 2026 wallet claim and cross-border bank layer; and where do finality, correction, insolvency and route evidence remain incomplete?
bluf: Mainland China does not operate a general licensed crypto market. The February 2026 eight-agency notice, which expressly repealed the 2021 notice, prohibits core virtual-currency business and unapproved RWA tokenization while preserving only exact authority-approved activity on specified financial infrastructure and imposing outbound controls. The separate e-CNY system moved to a 2.0 liability model on 1 January 2026: commercial-bank wallet balances are liabilities of the operating bank with interest, reserve treatment and deposit insurance, while nonbank wallet balances are provider liabilities backed by 100% guarantee funds; PBOC retains top-layer rules and infrastructure. The six large state-owned banks are both domestic systemically important banks and original operating institutions, but their customer and route evidence differs: CCB reports 30.05 million active personal wallets, 2.61 million active corporate wallets and 930,000 active merchants for 2025; PSBC reported more than 33 million wallets by mid-2025; ICBC, BOC, CCB, BoCom and PSBC disclose distinct smart-contract or cross-border receipts. BOC's July 2026 first-batch Singapore CBETS retail transactions correct the earlier signature-only state, but do not supply a complete payer-to-beneficiary finality chain. Private crypto remains prohibited. No route arc is authorized.

authority.summary: The NPC and State Council own primary law and administrative regulation. PBOC governs money, e-CNY top-layer infrastructure, payment systems and AML; NDRC owns mining controls; CSRC, NFRA and SAFE own securities/RWA, prudential/payment and foreign-exchange capacities within their remits; public-security, procuratorial and judicial bodies own investigation, adjudication, seizure and recovery. Digital RMB operating centers and bank/nonbank operators perform distinct infrastructure and customer-facing roles.
authority.boundary: Legislation, policy notice, infrastructure operation, operator approval, payment-system participation, criminal process and a completed transaction are separate capacities.

legal_objects.summary: The record separates physical RMB and PBOC settlement balances; commercial-bank e-CNY wallet deposits; nonbank-provider e-CNY wallet liabilities and guarantee funds; private virtual currencies; RWA tokens or token-like ownership, beneficial or creditor rights; conventional bank and payment balances; and CIPS or other payment-system records.
legal_objects.boundary: Public infrastructure, digital form or shared technology does not merge central-bank money, a bank deposit, provider liability, cryptoasset, asset-backed token or settlement entry.

permitted_activities.summary: Domestic fiat/crypto and crypto/crypto conversion, central-counterparty dealing, pricing/intermediation, token issuance and crypto financial products are prohibited, as are financial and payment services for them. Domestic RWA tokenization is prohibited unless the competent authority approves use of specified financial infrastructure. Offshore RMB-linked stablecoin issuance and specified offshore virtual-currency or RWA activity by mainland-controlled persons require Chinese consent, filing or supervision. e-CNY and conventional regulated payment activity proceed through separate approved operators and systems.
permitted_activities.boundary: A narrow authority-gated tokenization exception, offshore licence or ordinary bank/payment licence cannot be generalized into a mainland VASP permission.

entry_gates.summary: There is no general mainland VASP licensing lane. Bank-wallet e-CNY requires PBOC operator approval, central-system connection, completed business/technical preparation and customer go-live; nonbank service adds payment-institution, guarantee-fund and AML requirements. CBETS, mBridge/Jisr, CIPS and Payment Connect each require their own participant, account, liquidity, FX and use-case admissions.
entry_gates.boundary: Approval, system connection, preparation, contract signature, technical launch, first transaction and recurring production are separate clocks.

named_operating_actors.summary: PBOC had approved 30 bank-class e-CNY operators by 18 August 2026: the six large state-owned banks, China Merchants Bank, Industrial Bank, MYbank, WeBank, 12 banks added in April and eight added in August. The six large banks—ICBC, ABC, BOC, CCB, Bank of Communications and PSBC—also appear in the 2025 domestic systemically important bank list. New cohorts must finish preparation before service. Bank-specific evidence establishes that all six original operators have customer wallet or e-CNY application states, while BOC, ICBC, CCB, BoCom and PSBC disclose specific cross-border or smart-contract receipts. Digital RMB operating centers own domestic/international infrastructure; CBETS names 26 initial direct participants and BOC completed the first batch of Singapore retail transactions. CIPS reported 210 direct and 1,619 indirect participants at June 2026.
named_operating_actors.boundary: Approved operator, operating-center legal person, participant agreement, connected institution, active customer service and transaction scale are different facts.

claims_and_backing.summary: A commercial-bank e-CNY wallet is an account-based liability of that bank, may earn interest, enters its reserve base and receives deposit-equivalent insurance treatment. A nonbank wallet is the provider's liability backed by 100% e-CNY guarantee funds. Deposit insurance currently pays covered principal and interest up to CNY 500,000 per depositor aggregated at one insured institution, with excess claims in liquidation. Private virtual-currency losses may be self-borne when the civil act violates public order, while criminal tracing and restitution remain separate.
claims_and_backing.boundary: PBOC governance, bank liability, provider liability, required guarantee funds, deposit insurance, liquidation claim, criminal seizure and actual victim recovery are not interchangeable protections.

domestic_rails.summary: PBOC's large-value payment system and other conventional systems supply central-bank and bank-money processing; Q3 2025 large-value volume was 103 million transactions worth CNY 2,502.01 trillion. CIPS is a separate production cross-border RMB system. e-CNY 2.0 supplies bank/provider wallets under PBOC infrastructure, while Payment Connect links mainland bank infrastructure to Hong Kong FPS. A single public rulebook joining every 2.0 customer, operator, PBOC-record and finality clock was not located.
domestic_rails.boundary: Wallet debit, operator record, payment-system instruction, customer bank credit and final central-bank-money settlement may be separate events.

cross_border_routes.summary: The China-UAE joint statement records an AED 50 million first direct Digital Dirham payment through mBridge by June 2024; the November 2025 Jisr event was a later launch and transaction demonstration. Bank evidence goes beyond platform signatures: BOC completed the first batch of CBETS cross-border retail transactions for Singapore customers and says BOCHK became the first offshore e-CNY custodian; ICBC and CCB each report a first China-Singapore e-CNY application; BoCom reports CBETS direct-participant agreements for its Hong Kong, Macao and Brazil entities and a Malaysia inbound-wallet solution; PSBC reports online and offline mBridge enterprise use. Payment Connect is a production conventional fiat comparator. Public evidence still does not complete payer/payee identity, funding, FX, both currency legs, beneficiary credit, legal finality, correction or recurring bilateral volume for any one route.
cross_border_routes.boundary: Bilateral statement, platform launch, demonstration, participant signature, whole-program aggregate and recurring end-to-end corridor are different evidence states.

operating_state.summary: The e-CNY 2.0 framework is effective and e-CNY has material cumulative trial use; official materials still describe trial promotion/development rather than one completed statutory nationwide launch. The virtual-currency/RWA notice is effective. Thirty bank operators are approved but later cohorts may not all be customer-live. The original six large banks have direct current evidence of wallet services, 2.0 interest conversion or application receipts. CIPS and Payment Connect are production bank-money rails. CBETS moved beyond signatures when BOC completed first-batch Singapore customer transactions in July 2026, but public systemwide participant and volume data remain incomplete.
operating_state.boundary: Effective framework, trial use, statutory recognition, operator approval, customer service, platform capability, first transaction and recurring production must remain separate.

scale.summary: Through November 2025, official figures reported 3.48 billion cumulative e-CNY transactions worth CNY 16.7 trillion, 230 million personal wallets and 18.84 million corporate wallets. CCB alone reported 30.05 million active personal wallets, 2.61 million active corporate wallets and 930,000 active merchants for 2025; PSBC reported more than 33 million personal wallets through its app at June 2025, a different measure. mBridge reported 4,047 cross-border payments worth CNY 387.2 billion, with e-CNY at 95.3% of value across currencies. CIPS had 210 direct and 1,619 indirect participants at June 2026 and processed 791,000 transactions worth CNY 19.4 trillion in August. These populations and clocks cannot be added together.
scale.boundary: Cumulative pre-reform e-CNY use, approved operators, mBridge aggregate, CIPS participants and conventional payment volume are different denominators and do not establish route or active-user scale.

stress.summary: The 2026 notice cites renewed virtual-currency and RWA-tokenization speculation and establishes joined monitoring, service denial, internet, advertising, mining, local-enforcement and criminal-response mechanisms. Police cases show transaction tracing and individual recovery. No joined national series was located for crypto losses, seizures and restitution or for e-CNY outages, unauthorized transfers, operator failures, bank-wallet insolvencies or guarantee-fund losses.
stress.boundary: Policy concern, investigation, conviction, seizure, customer loss, system outage, insolvency and restitution are separate observed states.

correction_and_loss.summary: Correction may occur through wallet and credential controls, bank/provider books, e-CNY technical records, conventional payment-system procedures, provider complaint and compensation mechanisms, regulatory freeze/action, deposit insurance/liquidation or criminal/judicial recovery. The nonbank framework requires complaints, loss-compensation and exit plans; one police case records full CNY 200,000 recovery. No public e-CNY 2.0 rulebook or observed national recovery series joins these layers.
correction_and_loss.boundary: Technical adjustment, payment reversal, final interbank settlement, provider compensation, insured payout, confiscation and victim restitution have distinct clocks and authorities.

evidence_boundary.summary: The recertification uses current national instruments, PBOC-sourced operating notices, official infrastructure and six-large-bank data, judicial/police records and bounded existing Workbench owners. It preserves the 2021-to-2026 policy and e-CNY claim changes, corrects CBETS from agreement-only to bounded first-batch transactions, identifies republished rather than direct sources where necessary, and authorizes no route arc. No post-15 September crypto or e-CNY operating-state delta was found through the intraday cutoff.
evidence_boundary.boundary: Fresh research is not Chronicle promotion, watch creation, publication authority, investment advice, shared-surface shipment or permission to hand-edit generated files.
